title: ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini? The Three Big AI Chats at a Glance
excerpt: Three AI chats, three providers. What ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini can do according to their own pages, what is free, and how you find the right one for you.
body:
If you want to start with AI today, you almost always end up with one of three names: ChatGPT from OpenAI, Claude from Anthropic, and Gemini from Google. All three are chat assistants. You write a question or a task, and the AI answers. In everyday use they differ in the details, and those are exactly what we look at here. This is based on the providers’ official pages, which we visited on 1 November 2026.

ChatGPT can do a great deal at once. On the overview page, OpenAI describes several uses: writing and revising text, creating images from a description, and talking through ideas in voice mode when speaking is easier than typing. According to OpenAI, ChatGPT can also be connected to work apps such as Gmail and Slack.

The pricing page has a free plan called “Free” for 0 € a month. Above that are paid tiers with more messages, more uploads, and more image creation. The exact limits change from time to time, so it is worth looking at the current pricing page before you start a subscription.

Anthropic describes Claude this way: Give Claude a task, not just a question. The product page has many examples from everyday work, such as evaluating surveys, reviewing contracts, or preparing presentations. Claude is meant to work more like a colleague you hand a whole project to.

Claude also has a free plan for 0 €. Anthropic writes that use is limited every five hours and per week. If you need more, you can switch to Pro and higher tiers. A practical point: besides the web version, Anthropic also offers a desktop app, and the German page even mentions Linux explicitly.

Google calls Gemini the interface for a multimodal language model that can process text, audio, and images, among other things. On the overview page, Google lists features such as Gemini Live, image, video, and music generation, as well as Deep Research and Canvas.

An important notice sits right in the chat window: Gemini is an AI and can make mistakes, including with information about people. That applies to all three chats here, by the way.

To be honest: there is no clear winner. All three are being developed all the time, and what works better with one provider today can look different in three months. Instead of relying on rankings, run a small test of your own:

That way you find out in half an hour which assistant fits the way you work. And because all three let you start for free, the test costs you nothing but a little time.

ChatGPT is the versatile classic, Claude is built for whole tasks according to Anthropic, and Gemini handles images and audio as well as text. Try all three for free and decide based on your own tasks. You can find more AI chats in our tool directory.
seoTitle: ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini? The Three Big AI Chats
seoDescription: Three AI chats, three providers. What ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini can do according to their own pages, what is free, and how you find the right one for you.

title: Local AI: How a Chatbot Runs on Your Own Computer
excerpt: Want to use AI without your texts ending up in the cloud? With Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, and AnythingLLM, language models run directly on your computer.
body:
ChatGPT and the like run on the providers’ servers. Everything you type is sent over the internet. For many tasks that is no problem. If you work with private notes, customer data, or internal documents, another option is interesting: a language model that runs directly on your own computer.

That sounds complicated, but these days it hardly is. We introduce four programs you can start with in a few minutes. All details come from the official pages, visited on 1 November 2026.

The catch: local models need computing power. The larger the model, the more memory and graphics power your computer needs. For simple tasks such as summarizing, rephrasing, or brainstorming, smaller models are often enough.

Ollama is a tool for loading and running open language models, either locally or in the cloud. The project is under the MIT license and can be found on GitHub. It can be installed on macOS, Windows, and Linux. On its homepage, Ollama writes that prompts are neither stored nor used for training.

Ollama is aimed more at people who are not afraid of the command line. In return, it is the foundation for many other programs that use Ollama in the background.

LM Studio is a desktop app in which you download and use local models directly. Under the hood, according to the maker, llama.cpp and MLX do the work. The free “Free” plan covers running local models on your computer. There is also an agent called Bionic that helps with writing, programming, and automations. If you want more, you can optionally add paid cloud models.

Good to know: LM Studio is free, but it is not an open-source project in the narrow sense.

On GitHub, Jan describes itself as an open-source alternative to ChatGPT that runs 100 percent offline on your computer. The code is under the Apache-2.0 license. The interface resembles familiar chat apps, so Jan is a good start for anyone who simply wants to get going.

AnythingLLM goes one step further. Besides the chat, you can bring in your own documents, which then become your assistant’s knowledge, without data leaving the device. According to the maker, the app needs no account and no API key. It runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux and is under the MIT license.

If you run your own server, Open WebUI is interesting. It is a web interface you host yourself and connect to Ollama or to cloud providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic. That way the whole family or the team uses the same AI through the browser. To Open WebUI

Local AI is no substitute for the strongest cloud models, but it is a very good complement. For private texts, notes, and documents, you are on the safe side with it. You can find more open-source tools in our tool directory.
seoTitle: Local AI: How a Chatbot Runs on Your Own Computer
seoDescription: Want to use AI without your texts ending up in the cloud? With Ollama, LM Studio, Jan, and AnythingLLM, language models run directly on your computer.

title: Creating AI Images: Leonardo, Firefly, Krea, and Microsoft Designer at a Glance
excerpt: From a social media post to a product idea: four AI image generators, what they can do according to the providers, and what the free start offers.
body:
A picture from a few words: a few years ago that was still science fiction. Today there are dozens of image generators, and the choice is the problem more than the technology. We picked out four well-known tools and checked their official pages for what they offer. Details as of 1 November 2026.

You describe in a text field what you want to see. That description is called a prompt. The AI creates one or more images from it. The more precise your prompt, the closer the result comes to what you had in mind. Good prompts name:

Leonardo calls itself a generative AI platform for creatives. You create images from simple prompts or from your own models, and you can also set images in motion, turning them into small animations and videos.

The pricing page has a “Free” plan for 0 Dollar a month with 150 fast tokens per day. Important: on the free plan, your works are public, according to the pricing page. If you need private images, you end up on a paid plan.

Adobe describes Firefly as a creative AI studio. You generate and edit images, videos, audio, and designs. A special point: Firefly bundles not only Adobe’s own models but, according to Adobe, models from partners such as Google, OpenAI, and Kling AI as well. The German product page says “Start for free now”. If you already work with Photoshop or other Adobe programs, you will feel at home here quickly.

Krea is a kind of gathering place for image and video AI. On the homepage, next to the in-house model Krea 3, you also find models from other providers, plus tools for editing, upscaling, and real-time generation. The free plan offers 100 units per day, according to the pricing page.

Krea is worth it if you want to compare different models without opening a separate account for each one.

Microsoft Designer is less a professional tool and more a helper for quick design work. On the homepage, Designer asks: “What would you like to design?” The choices include images, invitations, banners, posters, posts for social networks, greeting cards, stickers, and coloring-book pages. You can create something new with AI, edit existing images with AI, or design from scratch yourself.

Before you use AI images for business, read the terms of use of the provider in question. There it says whether and how you may use the images commercially. And a tip in the name of fairness: do not create images of real people without their consent, and label AI images when they could be mistaken for real photos.

Leonardo, Firefly, and Krea mention a free way to start on their pages. With Microsoft Designer, you are best off checking the current terms right when you sign up. Start with a simple prompt, compare the results, and then decide whether a paid plan is worth it. You can find even more image AI in our tool directory.
seoTitle: AI Images: Leonardo, Firefly, Krea, and Microsoft Designer
seoDescription: From a social media post to a product idea: four AI image generators, what they can do according to the providers, and what the free start offers.

title: Creating AI Videos: Runway, Kling, Luma, and Hailuo for Beginners
excerpt: A sentence becomes a video clip. We show how text-to-video works and what Runway, Kling, Luma, and Hailuo offer according to their own information.
body:
Video AI has made huge leaps in a short time. Where a whole team with a camera used to be needed, a good description is often enough today for a short clip. In this post we explain the basics and introduce four well-known platforms. All details come from the official pages, visited on 1 November 2026.

With text-to-video you describe the scene in words, and the AI creates a short clip from that. With image-to-video you upload a photo or a graphic, and the AI sets it in motion. For beginners, image-to-video is often easier, because you already set the look and the AI only has to invent the movement.

Runway describes itself as a cloud-based creative platform where you create and edit videos, images, and audio in one workspace. It is aimed at individuals just as much as at teams.

The pricing page has a permanently free plan with 125 one-time credits to try out and 5 GB of storage. One-time means the credits do not refill every month.

Kling AI is a video and image generator. On the homepage, Kling introduces the model Kling 4.0, which according to the provider focuses on stable motion and on image and sound working together. There is also Kling Image 3.0 for still images that are meant to look cinematic. Kling also shows examples from advertising, music videos, and fashion online shops.

Luma relies on so-called creative agents that accompany you from the plan to the finished result. Its own video model is called Ray. According to Luma, Ray 3.2 gives you control frame by frame and keeps a consistent look. An interesting point: according to its own page, Luma also offers models from other providers, such as Kling, Veo, and MiniMax. The page says “Try for free”.

Hailuo runs video models from MiniMax, for example MiniMax H3 on the homepage. You describe in the text field which video you want, choose a model and a format, for example 21:9 for a cinematic look, and start the creation. Besides videos, there are image and audio tools there as well.

AI videos can look deceptively real in places. Do not create videos of real people without their permission, and label AI clips when they could be confused with real footage. Also check the provider’s terms to see whether you may use the clips commercially.

For a first test, Runway is a good fit with its free credits. If you are looking for cinematic results, take a look at Kling and Luma, and Hailuo is a good fit for quick experiments. You can find more video tools in our tool directory.
seoTitle: AI Videos for Beginners: Runway, Kling, Luma, and Hailuo
seoDescription: A sentence becomes a video clip. We show how text-to-video works and what Runway, Kling, Luma, and Hailuo offer according to their own information.

title: AI Coding Assistants: GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, and Cline Compared
excerpt: Programming with AI help: what GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, and the open-source tool Cline can do according to the providers, and what is free.
body:
AI assistants for programming have long been more than clever autocomplete. Many now work as so-called agents: you describe a task, and the AI changes several files on its own, runs commands, and proposes the result for you to review. We introduce four well-known tools. The basis is the official pages, visited on 1 November 2026.

Imagine a very fast intern who can read your project. You say, “Add a contact form,” and they find the right files, write the code, and show you the changes. You decide whether to accept them. That is exactly what coding agents do. What still matters: you are responsible for the code, and you should understand every change before you accept it.

GitHub Copilot is GitHub’s AI assistant. On the product page, GitHub describes Copilot as a coding agent that helps from individual tasks through to projects spanning several repositories. You can hand work over to Copilot and later continue in the Copilot app, in the terminal, in the editor, on github.com, or in GitHub Mobile. There is also a code review by the AI.

The pricing page has a “Free” plan for 0 US-Dollar that opens directly in Visual Studio Code. The paid tiers start at Pro.

Cursor describes itself as “your agent for building ambitious software”. It is its own code editor, which you download, and there is also a command-line version. You hand tasks to the agent and keep working on something else in the meantime. The pricing page lists a free plan with a limited number of agent and chat requests.

Anyone who opens windsurf.com today lands on “Devin Desktop” from the company Cognition. The idea: a command center where you manage several AI agents locally or in the cloud. The Windsurf pricing page still lists a “Free” plan for 0 Dollar with a small allowance for agents, unlimited inline edits, and unlimited tab completions.

Cline is the open-source candidate in this round. The project is on GitHub under the Apache-2.0 license. Cline runs as an extension in Visual Studio Code, JetBrains, Cursor, and Windsurf, and also in the terminal and as a desktop app.

The big advantage: you choose the AI model yourself. According to Cline, Claude, GPT, Gemini, local models via Ollama or LM Studio, and any OpenAI-compatible access all work. Cline works in two steps: first the AI plans with you, then it carries the plan out. You can approve each step on its own.

GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Windsurf have a free plan. Cline is open source, but for cloud models you may pay the model provider in question. Local models via Ollama or LM Studio cost nothing extra. Try two of them on a small project of your own. After one afternoon you will know which assistant fits your style. You can find more developer tools in our tool directory.
seoTitle: GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, and Cline Compared
seoDescription: Programming with AI help: what GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, and the open-source tool Cline can do according to the providers, and what is free.

title: DeepL or Google Translate? What the Two Translators Can Do
excerpt: Two translators, two strengths. We show what DeepL and Google Translate offer according to their own pages, and when each one is the better fit.
body:
An English email, a Spanish recipe, a contract in French: translators are among the most useful tools there are. Two very well-known ones are DeepL and Google Translate. Both can be used directly in the browser. We looked at what the providers themselves write about their services. As of 1 November 2026.

DeepL describes itself as an AI translation platform that translates texts, files, media formats, and speech. On the translator page you can paste text right away. You also drag PDF, Word (.docx), and PowerPoint (.pptx) files straight into the window to carry them over with the document translator. Among its most popular language pairs, DeepL itself counts English–German, French–German, and Spanish–German.

What is new is that, according to its own homepage, DeepL is also available via MCP in Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, and Claude. There is an API for developers.

There is also DeepL Write. That is not a translator but a writing helper that improves your texts. There is a free version of that as well.

Free and Pro: you can use the basic features at no charge. The “DeepL Pro” subscription starts in Germany with the “Individual” package and, according to the pricing page, can be tried free for 30 days. In the paid package, DeepL explicitly says that your data is not used for model training. For confidential business texts, that is an important point.

Google Translate shows its strengths above all on the smartphone. On the official info page, Google mentions, among other things:

DeepL offers a free translator, and you open Google Translate directly in the browser or in the app. The two complement each other well. DeepL is your tool at the desk, and Google Translate is your companion on the go. Many people simply use both. You can find more language tools in our tool directory.
seoTitle: DeepL or Google Translate? What the Two Translators Can Do
seoDescription: Two translators, two strengths. We show what DeepL and Google Translate offer according to their own pages, and when each one is the better fit.

title: Spell Checking with AI: LanguageTool, Duden-Mentor, and Grammarly
excerpt: Commas, typos, clumsy sentences: three writing helpers at a glance, with what they can do for free and on a subscription according to the providers.
body:
A comma in the wrong place, a “das” instead of “dass”, a sentence that simply does not sound right: everyone knows that. Writing helpers with AI find those spots in seconds. For German texts there are three names you keep coming across. Here is what the providers themselves say, as of 1 November 2026.

LanguageTool describes itself as AI-based checking for commas, grammar, and spelling that corrects texts in many languages and rephrases them if you want. On the German site, German is first among the recommended languages.

What is especially practical is everywhere LanguageTool runs along:

You can paste text directly on the website and have it checked. With a free account you also get a personal dictionary, a distraction-free writing mode, and text statistics. If you want unlimited rephrasing, you can switch to Premium.

Interesting for tech fans: according to GitHub, the core of LanguageTool is open source under the LGPL 2.1 license or later.

Everyone knows the name Duden from school. On duden.de there is Duden-Mentor, which helps you correct your texts. You can try it directly on the site. With a Premium subscription, according to Duden, you also get synonym suggestions, tips on writing style, and further features. There are separate offers for companies.

Grammarly calls itself an AI partner that turns your thoughts into clear text. Besides the classic correction of grammar, sentence structure, and clarity, there are extra features such as a “Humanizer”, which is meant to give texts more personality, and an AI detector that finds AI-generated passages.

The pricing page has a “Free” plan for 0 € a month, with which you write without spelling and grammar errors and are shown your tone. Pro can be tried for free. Grammarly also writes that users’ content is not sold and is not used for advertising.

Grammarly’s site and examples are geared toward English. If you mainly write German texts, test beforehand whether it suits you.

For most German texts, LanguageTool is a very good start, because it runs for free in the browser, in Word, and in email programs. Duden-Mentor is the choice for Duden fans, and Grammarly is the choice for anyone who writes a lot in English. You can find more writing tools in our tool directory.
seoTitle: AI Spell Check: LanguageTool, Duden-Mentor, and Grammarly
seoDescription: Commas, typos, clumsy sentences: three writing helpers at a glance, with what they can do for free and on a subscription according to the providers.

title: NotebookLM (Now Gemini Notebook): A Beginner’s Guide
excerpt: Upload PDFs, web pages, or videos and ask questions about them, with a source citation in every line. How Google’s research assistant works, step by step.
body:
Imagine you have ten PDFs, three YouTube videos, and a few web pages on a topic, and you want to know what is in them without reading everything. That is exactly what Google built NotebookLM for. Google now offers the tool under the name Gemini Notebook. Anyone who opens the old address notebooklm.google is redirected to the new page. All details in this post come from Google’s official page and from Google Help, visited on 1 November 2026.

Google calls it an AI-based research assistant. The most important difference from a normal AI chat: according to Google, the answers are based on the information you provide yourself. So you are working with your own sources, not with the entire internet. That makes the answers easier to trace.

According to Google Help, you can add these sources, among others:

You can also discover new sources on your topic inside the tool.

Step 1: Create a notebook. Open Gemini Notebook and create a new notebook. A notebook is like a folder for one topic, for example “term paper on climate change” or “vacation in Portugal”.

Step 2: Add sources. Upload your files or add links. The better your sources, the better the answers.

Step 3: Ask questions. Type your question into the chat field. According to Google, the answer includes source citations right in the relevant line. You immediately see which document a statement comes from, and you can check it.

Step 4: Transform your sources. In Help, Google names several formats you can turn your sources into: exam-preparation materials, source overviews, audio summaries, and mind maps.

With the audio summaries, according to Google, you have an overview of your sources read aloud, and it is interactive. That is perfect on the go: instead of reading ten PDFs, you listen to a summary on the train.

Google Help itself gives a few good tips:

If you do not have an idea of your own, you will find recommended public notebooks to try on the homepage. According to Google Help, Gemini Notebook currently supports over 80 languages.
seoTitle: NotebookLM (Now Gemini Notebook): A Beginner’s Guide
seoDescription: Upload PDFs, web pages, or videos and ask questions about them, with a source citation in every line. How Google’s research assistant works, step by step.

title: Scientific Research with AI: 5 Tools for Study and Research
excerpt: Find scholarly articles, summarize them, and see how a research field fits together: five research tools you can try for free.
body:
For a term paper or a thesis you need good sources. Google only helps up to a point, and a general AI, in the worst case, invents studies that do not exist at all. Specialized research tools work with real scholarly databases. We introduce five of them. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

Elicit describes itself as AI for scientific research. You enter a research question, Elicit searches academic papers, and on request it creates a structured report with citations.

The free “Basic” plan includes, according to the pricing page:

The Research Agent and the Research Reports can be used only to a limited extent on the free plan. Paid plans are aimed at people who do systematic reviews.

Consensus searches and analyzes peer-reviewed scholarly literature. According to the provider, agents read the papers, pull out the data, and back every statement with a source. You can, for example, have a short summary or a comparison table built for you.

On the free plan for 0 $ you get basic paper search, 10 Pro messages a month, and up to 3 “Deep Reviews” a month. With a free account you can save your work and build a library of your own.

Semantic Scholar is developed by a team at Ai2 and, in its own words, offers free, AI-supported search and discovery tools for research. More than 200 million scholarly works from every field are indexed. There is an API for developers.

Semantic Scholar is a good starting point if you simply want to know which works exist on a topic.

Connected Papers takes a different path. You enter a paper, for example by DOI, arXiv link, PubMed link, or title, and you get a visual graph of similar works.

According to the provider, around 50,000 papers are analyzed for this, and the few dozen with the strongest connection to the starting paper are selected. Important: it is not simply a citation tree. The similarity is based on shared citations and bibliographic references. Papers can therefore sit close together even when they do not cite each other directly.

ResearchRabbit analyzes papers you like and suggests research you have overlooked so far. Signing up is free, according to the website.
seoTitle: Scientific Research with AI: 5 Tools for Study and Research
seoDescription: Find scholarly articles, summarize them, and see how a research field fits together: five research tools you can try for free.

title: Never Write Minutes Again: 4 AI Meeting Assistants Compared
excerpt: Otter, Fireflies, tl;dv, and Notta take notes in Zoom, Teams, and Google Meet and summarize them. What the providers’ free plans include.
body:
If you take notes in a meeting, you only half listen. AI meeting assistants take that off your hands: they transcribe the conversation, recognize speakers, and at the end summarize what was discussed. We looked at four well-known services. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026. Prices and limits change often, so check once more yourself before you start.

In its own words, Otter wants to do more than notes. The tool prepares you before the appointment, gives live hints during the conversation, and afterward sends automatic follow-ups into your tools.

The free “Basic” plan includes, according to the pricing page, among other things:

According to the website, Fireflies transcribes, summarizes, searches, and analyzes your team’s conversations. It names more than 100 languages, speaker recognition, and automatic speech recognition from meeting to meeting.

The “Free” plan is permanently free according to the provider and includes:

According to the website, tl;dv captures meeting notes in 30 languages, updates your CRM if you want, and drafts the next follow-up email. Of interest to users in Germany: tl;dv advertises that it is GDPR-compliant and that it hosts and stores data in the EU.

The free plan for 0 € needs no credit card and, according to the pricing page, includes unlimited video recordings and unlimited transcription in more than 30 languages.

According to the website, Notta transcribes, summarizes, and directly creates slides, infographics, and task lists. 58 languages are supported. Notta also calls itself GDPR-compliant.

The Free plan for 0 € (no credit card) includes, according to the pricing page, 120 transcription minutes a month, but only up to 3 minutes per conversation. On top of that come 50 file uploads and 10 AI summaries a month. That is enough for a try. For long meetings, it is less so.

Before you have a meeting recorded, everyone taking part has to know and agree. In Germany that is not only polite, it is legally important as well. A short sentence at the start is often enough: “Is it okay if my assistant takes notes?”

title: Creating Songs with AI: Suno and Udio Compared
excerpt: A song for a birthday, a jingle for a video, or simply trying it out: how Suno and Udio differ, and what you need to watch for with the rights.
body:
Write a song of your own without playing an instrument? AI music generators make that possible: you describe what you want to hear, and after a short while you get a finished track with vocals. The two best-known services are Suno and Udio. We show what both offer according to their own websites. As of 1 November 2026.

Suno promises: “Make any song you can imagine”. You start with a simple description or go deeper into the editing tools. Whether it is a melody in your head, lyrics of your own, or just a feeling, according to Suno that is enough as a starting point.

What else Suno mentions:

Free tier according to the pricing page: 0 € a month, access to the free models, 50 credits per day, and uploads of up to 8 minutes of audio. The limits matter: no monthly song downloads, no commercial rights, and no stem separation. Commercial usage rights start only with the Pro tier.

Udio promotes the idea of creating the soundtrack of your life: a ballad for the romantic date, a party song for an evening with friends, a lo-fi track for meditating, or a cheerful song for a children’s birthday party. If you can describe it in words, according to Udio you can also express it as music.

For more advanced users, Udio names tools such as extending a track (Extend), targeted fixes to individual spots (Inpaint), Remix, and uploading songs of your own.

Free plan according to the pricing page: 0 $ a month, with no credit card. You get 10 credits per day and 100 credits per month, which do not carry over. You can generate up to 4 songs at once, but at most 3 full-length songs (2:10 minutes) per day.

A good prompt describes the music the way you would describe it to a friend:

Example: “Cheerful acoustic pop with a female voice, about a summer day at the lake.”

If you want to use a song on YouTube, Instagram, or in an ad video, you have to read the terms of use carefully. With Suno, commercial rights are explicitly excluded on the free tier. With Udio, too, you should check which rights your plan includes before you publish. And: do not use other artists’ lyrics or voices without permission.

Suno and Udio make music accessible to everyone. For fun in between, the free offers are quite enough. If you want to use songs commercially, you need a paid tier and should read the terms carefully. You can find more audio tools in our tool directory.
seoTitle: Creating Songs with AI: Suno and Udio Compared
seoDescription: A song for a birthday, a jingle for a video, or simply trying it out: how Suno and Udio differ, and what you need to watch for with the rights.

title: Have Text Read Aloud: 4 AI Voice Tools for Audiobooks, Video, and Daily Life
excerpt: Listen to PDFs instead of reading them, a voiceover for the next video, or simply accessibility: ElevenLabs, Murf, Speechify, and NaturalReader at a glance.
body:
Modern AI voices stopped sounding like a robot a long time ago. You can have long articles read aloud, create a voiceover for your YouTube video, or listen to study material on the go. For people with reading difficulties or visual impairments, tools like these are a real help. We introduce four well-known services. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

ElevenLabs offers far more than reading aloud: text-to-speech, speech recognition, voice cloning, dubbing, sound effects, and even music. According to the homepage, there is expressive speech in more than 90 languages. Brand new is the model Eleven v4, which ElevenLabs calls its most emotional so far.

Free plan according to the pricing page: 10,000 credits per month, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, sound effects, Voice Design, music, and 3 projects in Studio. A commercial license and fast voice cloning (“Instant Voice Cloning”) are listed only on the paid Starter plan.

Murf is aimed at companies, developers, and creators. There is a studio for AI voiceovers and an interface (API) for your own applications, for example voice agents.

For the API, according to the pricing page, there is a free trial with no credit card and 10 $ in starting credit. More than 150 voices in over 35 languages and styles are mentioned. After that you pay by usage.

In its own words, Speechify reads PDFs, documents, and more aloud to you with natural-sounding voices, highlights the text as it goes, summarizes it, or turns it into a podcast. New is a dictation feature for writing by voice. There are apps for iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac, and Windows, plus extensions for Chrome and Edge and a web app.

Free plan according to the pricing page: reading aloud at up to 1.5 times speed, 10 rather robotic-sounding voices, and only the text-to-speech features. The natural voices, more than 60 languages, and higher speeds are in the Premium subscription.

According to the website, NaturalReader turns texts, PDFs, images, web pages, and even printed books into natural-sounding audio. In the online reader you can choose a language, including German (Germany). There are offers for private individuals, for commercial voiceovers, and for schools. You can start for free.

Clone only your own voice, or the voice of people who have expressly agreed. Using someone else’s voice without permission can have legal consequences, and it is simply unfair. Also check, before you publish, whether your plan allows commercial use.

For listening to texts, the free versions of Speechify or NaturalReader are often enough. For high-quality voiceovers, ElevenLabs is a strong choice. You can find more audio tools in our tool directory.
seoTitle: 4 AI Voice Tools for Audiobooks, Video, and Daily Life
seoDescription: Listen to PDFs instead of reading them, a voiceover for the next video, or simply accessibility: ElevenLabs, Murf, Speechify, and NaturalReader at a glance.

title: Free Instead of Expensive: 6 Open-Source Programs for Image, Video, Sound, and Office
excerpt: Image editing, vector graphics, office, video editing, audio, and 3D: six free programs that do not cost you a cent and do without a subscription.
body:
Many programs today cost a monthly subscription. For almost every task, though, there is free software you can download at no cost and use without limits. Behind these programs there are often large communities of volunteers. Here are six classics. All details come from the official project pages, as of 1 November 2026.

GIMP stands for “GNU Image Manipulation Program”. According to the project page, it is an image editor for photo retouching, image composition, and creating graphics. It runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, and other operating systems, and it is under the GNU General Public License. You may therefore view the source code, change it, and pass it on. Many settings and third-party plugins make GIMP very adaptable.

Inkscape calls itself a powerful, free design tool for vector graphics. It is aimed at illustrators, designers, web designers, and anyone who wants to design a logo or an icon, for example. The website mentions flexible drawing tools, a strong text tool, and support for many file formats.

A nice side note: according to its own announcement from May 2026, the Inkscape project supports a German petition that wants open-source work recognized as volunteer service.

LibreOffice is an open-source office suite. According to the website, you get six programs in one package:

LibreOffice is developed by a community with hundreds of contributors worldwide. The current version is LibreOffice 26.8.

Kdenlive stands for “KDE Non-Linear Video Editor” and, according to the website, runs on Linux, Windows, macOS, and BSD. It supports you from simple cuts through to an elaborate project: multicamera editing, nested sequences, markers, and automatic backups. You can create subtitles with automatic transcription.

Audacity calls itself the world’s most popular free software for recording and editing audio. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux and supports all common audio formats. Asked whether Audacity is free, the team answers: yes, and that it will stay that way. The current version is called Audacity 4.

Blender is free open-source software for 3D graphics and is under the GNU GPL. According to its own mission, the Blender Foundation has set out to put the best 3D technology, as free software, into the hands of artists.

With these six programs you cover image, graphics, office, video, audio, and 3D, with no subscription at all. You can find more free programs in our tool directory.
seoTitle: 6 Open-Source Programs for Image, Video, Sound, and Office
seoDescription: Image editing, vector graphics, office, video editing, audio, and 3D: six free programs that do not cost you a cent and do without a subscription.

title: Remove Backgrounds with AI: remove.bg, Photoroom, Clipdrop, and Pixelcut
excerpt: Cut out a product photo, spruce up a profile picture, make stickers: four tools that remove backgrounds automatically. Plus: what is changing at remove.bg.
body:
Cutting a subject out used to be tedious work with the magic wand and the lasso. Today you upload a photo, and seconds later the background is gone. That is useful for product photos in an online shop, for job-application photos, presentations, or social media posts. We introduce four tools. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

For many people, remove.bg is the classic. According to a notice on the website, though, background removal from remove.bg is moving to Canva. The standalone website will no longer be available from 1 December 2026 at 9:00. According to the website footer, remove.bg is a brand of Canva Austria GmbH.

Until then you can still use the site as usual: upload an image or drag it in, and according to the provider the background is removed 100 percent automatically, in about five seconds. On the pricing page, remove.bg already points to Canva, where the feature is offered free to try in HD.

Our tip: if you use remove.bg regularly, for example via the API or a plugin, check now how things continue for you after 1 December.

Photoroom is aimed above all at online retail. According to the website, you turn product photos into images and videos for your listings. That includes a Background Remover, AI shadows, AI backgrounds, AI models for fashion, and a new Video Ad Maker that makes ad videos from product photos.

According to the homepage, you can get started for free. The paid tiers Pro and Max can be tried for free. Photoroom shows its prices in euros.

According to the website, Clipdrop now belongs to Jasper. It offers a collection of image tools. Among them are:

Pixelcut calls itself an AI platform for images and videos, aimed at sellers. A “Creative Agent” plans tasks and carries them out for you, for example lifestyle photos for a new collection.

The free plan includes, according to the pricing page, limited background removal, limited upscaling, and exports without a watermark. Unlimited cutouts and a commercial license appear only on the paid plans.

Edit only images you have the rights to, and ask people before you publish their photo. If you use images for business, check whether your plan allows commercial use. With Pixelcut, for example, the commercial license is listed explicitly with the paid plans.

For a quick cutout, the free offers are usually enough. For online retailers, Photoroom and Pixelcut are worth a look. If you have been relying on remove.bg, you should switch over in good time because of the move to Canva. You can find more image tools in our tool directory.
seoTitle: Remove Backgrounds: remove.bg, Photoroom, Clipdrop, Pixelcut
seoDescription: Cut out a product photo, spruce up a profile picture, make stickers: four tools that remove backgrounds automatically. Plus: what is changing at remove.bg.

title: Rescue Blurry Photos: 4 AI Upscalers for Enlarging Images
excerpt: An old phone photo, a logo that is too small, a pixelated image for print: these AI tools enlarge images and bring details back. From free to professional.
body:
A lovely photo, but unfortunately tiny or blurry? There used to be nothing you could do. An AI upscaler today does more than enlarge images: it fills in details that are missing. The result is often surprisingly sharp. We introduce four tools, from free to professional. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

Upscayl is an AI upscaler you install on your own computer. According to the website, the desktop app is available for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Upscayl calls itself “Free and Open Source”, with the motto: download once, yours forever. On GitHub the project is under the AGPL-3.0 license.

The website advertises up to 16 times higher resolution and several models for different kinds of images. Also new is an online service called Upscayl Cloud. What it costs is on Upscayl’s pricing page.

Let’s Enhance runs directly in the browser and, according to the website, offers three features:

You can edit up to 20 images at once. When you sign up you get free credits, and according to the pricing page a credit card is not required. On free access you scale up to 8 megapixels, and the images carry a watermark. That drops away only for paying users.

A piece of news that surprises many people: the website says “Freepik is now Magnific”. Magnific sees itself as a creative platform with many AI models for video, image, and audio. Upscaling to 4K and video upscaling are among the features named.

According to the pricing page, the Magnific upscalers for image and video are included in the Premium tier. It also says that your data is not used for model training, and a commercial AI license is included.

According to the website, Topaz Gigapixel from Topaz Labs enlarges almost any image by a factor of 6. It runs on Mac and Windows, as a standalone program or as a plugin. Besides upscaling, Topaz names lossless zoom, restoration, and restoring faces. Gigapixel is also part of the larger Topaz Studio package.

Topaz offers Gigapixel on a subscription, with unlimited local and cloud rendering.

An upscaler does not show “real” details that were not in the original. It guesses how the image probably looked. For keepsake photos, that is wonderful. An image edited this way does not hold up as evidence or as a document.

For most people, Upscayl is quite enough, because it is free and it works on your computer. If you want to stay in the browser, try Let’s Enhance. Professionals should look at Topaz and Magnific. You can find more image tools in our tool directory.
seoTitle: Rescue Blurry Photos: 4 AI Upscalers for Enlarging Images
seoDescription: An old phone photo, a logo that is too small, a pixelated image for print: these AI tools enlarge images and bring details back. From free to professional.

title: Zapier, Make, or n8n? Automation Explained for Beginners
excerpt: A new email, a new spreadsheet row, a message in the team chat: automation tools run flows like these on their own. How Zapier, Make, and n8n differ.
body:
Saving attachments from emails every day, copying form data into a spreadsheet, telling colleagues about new orders: an automation tool can take over routine work like this. You set once what should happen, and from then on it runs by itself. The three best-known tools for this are Zapier, Make, and n8n. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

The principle is the same for all three:

Several steps in a row make a workflow. By now, all three tools can also build in AI steps and AI agents.

Zapier talks about “automation in the age of agents”. According to the website, you get access to more than 9,000 apps. With Zapier MCP you connect AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor to your apps, and you can start and test workflows directly in the chat.

Free plan according to the pricing page: permanently free, with 100 tasks per month. Included are unlimited Zaps, Tables, and Forms, but only two-step Zaps, meaning one trigger and one action.

Make shows automations and AI agents on a visual canvas. You build workflows by drag and drop, by prompt, or from Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI chats. According to the website, more than 3,500 apps can be connected directly, and if you want, you can refine steps with JavaScript or Python.

At Make, a workflow is called a “scenario”. Billing is in credits: most actions cost one credit.

Free plan according to the website: no credit card required, no time limit, and according to the FAQ 1,000 credits per month.

n8n calls itself a platform for agents and workflows you can follow: you open each step and see what it does. According to the website, there are more than 500 built-in integrations, plus any API via HTTP and agents via MCP. One thing that sets it apart: you can run n8n on your own server.

Prices according to the pricing page: the hosted plans start at Starter with 20 € a month on yearly billing and 2,500 workflow executions. Starter and Pro can be tried for free without a credit card. You are billed by executions, no matter how many steps a workflow has.

On the license: n8n is not simply “free for everything”. In the documentation, n8n refers to a “Sustainable Use License” and an “n8n Community License”. Read these terms before you host n8n yourself, especially if you want to use it for business.
seoTitle: Zapier, Make, or n8n? Automation Explained for Beginners
seoDescription: A new email, a new spreadsheet row, a message in the team chat: automation tools run flows like these on their own. How Zapier, Make, and n8n differ.

title: Create Presentations with AI: Beautiful.ai, Pitch, Decktopus, and Plus AI
excerpt: From a keyword to a finished presentation in minutes: four AI tools compared, with free options and tips so your talk still sounds like you.
body:
A blank slide and little time: everyone who has to build presentations knows that. AI tools create a first draft for you from a few sentences, with structure, text, and design. After that you only have to refine it. We introduce four tools that work in different ways. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

Beautiful.ai is aimed above all at teams whose presentations should look consistent. The special feature is “Smart Slides”: according to the website, there are more than 300 layouts that align themselves automatically when you add content. You set brand colors, fonts, and logos once, and the slides adapt. You can start with AI or with a template.

Beautiful.ai offers a free trial.

Pitch focuses on working together: instead of each person working with the AI on their own, Pitch brings the team into a shared workspace. According to the website, the generated slides are fully editable. New are an MCP interface and an API, with which you can create presentations from your AI tools.

Free plan according to the pricing page: permanently free for 1 to 5 people. You get unlimited presentations, templates of your own, links for sharing, 2 external guests, and 100 AI credits. The credits do not renew after they are used up.

Decktopus promises the simplest start: you describe your topic, and according to the website the AI creates a complete presentation with structure, content, and design. You do not have to fill in a template or format each slide on its own. With the “Loop” feature you can also practice your talk.

The pricing page puts the Pro plan at the center. It includes 750 AI credits per month, which according to the provider comes to about 150 slides, plus export as PDF, PPT, and PNG.

Plus AI takes a different path. It is not a presentation program of its own, but an AI assistant for PowerPoint and Google Slides. You start with a short description or upload a file, such as a PDF, a Word document, a PowerPoint file, or a text file. After that you can rewrite and redesign individual slides with AI.

According to the pricing page, every plan starts with a 7-day trial with 1,000 AI credits.

If you upload confidential company data, check beforehand whether your employer allows it, and read the provider’s privacy notice.

With presentations, AI takes away the fear of the blank slide. You still bring the finishing touches and the story behind them. Start with Pitch’s free plan or a trial of the other tools. You can find more productivity tools in our tool directory.
seoTitle: AI Presentations: Beautiful.ai, Pitch, Decktopus, Plus AI
seoDescription: From a keyword to a finished presentation in minutes: four AI tools compared, with free options and tips so your talk still sounds like you.

title: Chat with PDFs: 4 AI Tools for Long Documents Compared
excerpt: A manual, a study, or a contract: upload the PDF and simply ask questions. ChatPDF, Humata, AskYourPDF, and PDF.ai, with their free limits.
body:
An 80-page PDF, and you only need one answer: What does it say about the notice period? How do I reset the device? What is the result of this study? With PDF chat tools you upload the file and ask your question in ordinary words. We looked at four services. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

ChatPDF describes itself as “PDF AI – like ChatGPT, but for PDFs”. The website is available in German. You drag a file into the window or paste text and links, and then ask your question. According to the website, you can chat not only with files but also with videos and websites. Summaries and answers are free, according to the provider. If you register for free, your chat history is saved.

ChatPDF also offers further tools such as flashcards, slides, an AI writer, and an AI detector. There is a desktop app and a mobile app.

Humata is aimed at teams that have to search through many documents. According to the website, you can summarize findings, compare documents, and search for answers across all your files. The answers come with citations that lead straight into the original file. That way you see where a statement comes from.

The free plan includes, according to the pricing page, the basic features for up to 60 free pages.

AskYourPDF today offers more than PDF chat alone, such as a website chatbot and an assistant that fills in PDF forms automatically. For classic document chat, the pricing page names these limits on the free plan:

PDF.ai offers a chat for PDFs and an interface for developers who want to turn documents into structured data: headings, paragraphs, tables, and fields such as names, dates, or amounts.

The “Hobby” plan is permanently free, according to the pricing page. It allows one PDF upload, 100 questions a month, and files up to 10 MB. A Chrome extension is included.

Contracts, doctor’s letters, or bank statements contain personal data. Before you upload something like that, read the provider’s privacy notice and consider whether to black out sensitive passages first. And, very important: an AI answer is no substitute for legal or tax advice.

PDF chat tools save a lot of reading time, especially with long documents. The free plans are enough to start with. Always check important answers against the original passage. You can find more tools for text in our tool directory.
seoTitle: Chat with PDFs: 4 AI Tools for Long Documents Compared
seoDescription: A manual, a study, or a contract: upload the PDF and simply ask questions. ChatPDF, Humata, AskYourPDF, and PDF.ai, with their free limits.

title: AI from Europe: 4 Providers You Should Know
excerpt: Not every good AI comes from the USA. Mistral, Aleph Alpha, Langdock, and DeepL build on European roots and data sovereignty. An overview.
body:
When people talk about AI, the names that come up are usually from the USA. There are strong providers in Europe as well. For many companies, public authorities, and private individuals, that matters: Where is my data processed? Who has control? We introduce four European providers. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

According to its own company history, Mistral’s founders wanted to create a different kind of AI company: a European pioneer that joins the latest technology with openness, transparency, cost efficiency, and responsibility. Mistral offers so-called open-weight models that companies can use unchanged or adapt to their needs.

What is interesting for everyday use is the assistant: the former product page for Le Chat now redirects to Vibe. Mistral describes Vibe as an AI agent for longer tasks that works with your knowledge and your tools. Examples on the website are meeting briefings, research, or summarizing unread emails. There is a free plan for quick answers and simple tasks, and a Pro plan for more complex work. For companies, Mistral cites full data residency in any cloud or any data center.

Aleph Alpha has sites in Heidelberg, Berlin, Bayreuth, and Munich. According to the website, the company develops specialized, sovereign language models and solutions together with organizations. The goal: the organization keeps control, and the AI adapts to its context.

New is Kolibri, a sovereign model for the public sector that, according to the website, you can use directly via an API.

Langdock is based in Berlin and wants to help companies introduce AI securely across the whole organization. The platform brings together a chat, workflows for automations, and AI agents. According to the website, the chat is model-agnostic: you are not tied to one provider, and you can use leading models.

On security, Langdock cites hosting in the EU, GDPR compliance, ISO 27001, and SOC 2 Type II. The platform runs, as you choose, managed, in your own cloud, or on your own servers.

According to the pricing page, you can try Langdock free for 7 days, with no credit card and with 5 € in AI model credit.

According to its own company page, DeepL was founded in Cologne in 2017. The service is known for its translations of texts and documents. There is also the writing helper DeepL Write. On the paid DeepL Pro tier, the provider commits to not using your data for model training. You can read more about that in our comparison of DeepL and Google Translate.

But take care: “from Europe” does not automatically mean “privacy-compliant for your purpose”. Always read the terms and the privacy notices yourself, and clarify inside the company which data may go into which tool.

European AI has long been a real alternative. For private individuals, Mistral Vibe’s free plan is the simplest way in. For companies, Langdock and Aleph Alpha are worth a look. You can find more providers in our tool directory.
seoTitle: AI from Europe: 4 Providers You Should Know
seoDescription: Not every good AI comes from the USA. Mistral, Aleph Alpha, Langdock, and DeepL build on European roots and data sovereignty. An overview.

title: The Best Notes App for You: Obsidian, Notion, Logseq, and AppFlowy
excerpt: Local and private, or in the cloud for the team? Four popular notes apps compared, with free offers, privacy, and open-source options.
body:
Ideas, to-dos, recipes, study material, meeting notes: it all has to go somewhere. A good notes app quickly becomes a second brain. The apps differ a great deal, though, especially on the question of where your notes are stored. We compare four popular apps. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

Obsidian describes itself as a free and flexible app for your private thoughts. According to the website, Obsidian stores the notes privately on your device. You can get to them quickly even offline, and nobody else can read them, not even Obsidian itself.

With thousands of plugins and an open API, you adapt the app to the way you work. Popular examples are a calendar for daily notes, or kanban boards.

Cost according to the pricing page: free, with no limits and no sign-up. Add-on services such as Sync (synchronization between devices with end-to-end encryption) and Publish (publishing notes on the web) cost extra. According to the FAQ, you do not have to buy a license for professional use either. There is a voluntary commercial license with which you can support development.

Notion is more than a notes app. It is a workspace for teams, with pages, databases, forms, and websites. Notion leans strongly on AI: according to the website, you find answers with citations and you automate routine work with agents.

Free plan according to the pricing page: for individuals who want to organize private projects and their life. Included are a trial of Notion AI, simple forms and websites, Notion Calendar, and databases with subtasks and custom properties.

On GitHub, Logseq calls itself an open-source platform for knowledge management and collaboration, with a focus on privacy, longevity, and control by users. The license is AGPL-3.0.

According to the website, Logseq is permanently free for private use. Your data belongs to you and stays locally with you. The notes are Markdown files, which you can also open with other programs. There are apps for iOS and Android, more than 150 plugins, and features such as task management, PDF annotations, and flashcards for studying.

On GitHub, AppFlowy calls itself an “Open Source Alternative To Notion”, also under AGPL-3.0. The app brings projects, wikis, and teams together, with AI search, a knowledge base, and AI meeting notes.

The special point: you can host AppFlowy yourself, on your own infrastructure, in your cloud, or even completely sealed off from the internet. AppFlowy talks about complete data sovereignty and also names local AI as an option. According to the website, you can start for free as well.

If you care about privacy, Obsidian or Logseq will serve you well. Teams feel at home in Notion, and if you want Notion features on your own servers, take a look at AppFlowy. You can find more productivity tools in our tool directory.

seoDescription: Local and private, or in the cloud for the team? Four popular notes apps compared, with free offers, privacy, and open-source options.

title: Edit Videos Without a Subscription: 5 Free Editing Programs
excerpt: From a vacation video to a YouTube channel: DaVinci Resolve, CapCut, Shotcut, Kdenlive, and Clipchamp cost nothing in the basic version. How they differ.
body:
Good video editing does not have to be expensive. There are programs that cost nothing in the basic version and can still do a lot. Some are more for professionals, others for a quick clip in between. We introduce five. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

DaVinci Resolve from Blackmagic Design is currently available in version 21. According to the maker, it combines editing, color correction, visual effects, motion graphics, audio post-production, and now photo editing as well, in a single program. Blackmagic stresses that these are the same tools used in Hollywood.

There is a free version to download and a paid version called DaVinci Resolve Studio.

CapCut is available as a desktop program, as an online editor, and as an app for your phone. According to the website, it offers numerous AI features: automatic subtitles, speech output, noise reduction, removing image and video backgrounds, and image and video generators. You can download the desktop version for free.

According to its own website, Shotcut is a free, open-source video editor that runs on several operating systems. Thanks to FFmpeg, it supports many current audio and video formats. You can mix resolutions and frame rates in one project, record from a webcam, and create, import, and edit subtitles, for example in SRT or VTT format.

Kdenlive comes from the KDE community and, according to the website, runs on Linux, Windows, macOS, and BSD. It offers multicamera editing, nested sequences, markers, and automatic backups. You can create subtitles with automatic transcription.

Microsoft Clipchamp is an online video editor. According to the pricing page, you only need a personal Microsoft account. Payments or downloads are not required. The premium features are now included in the Microsoft 365 Single and Microsoft 365 Family subscriptions. If you already have a subscription like that, you get them at no extra charge.

For the first steps, Clipchamp or CapCut is enough. If you want to work with free open-source software, go for Shotcut or Kdenlive. And if you want to edit professionally over the long term, learn DaVinci Resolve. You can find more video tools in our tool directory.

seoDescription: From a vacation video to a YouTube channel: DaVinci Resolve, CapCut, Shotcut, Kdenlive, and Clipchamp cost nothing in the basic version. How they differ.

title: Videos Without a Camera: AI Avatars with Synthesia, HeyGen, and D-ID
excerpt: An explainer video, a training, or a social media clip, spoken by a digital avatar: how Synthesia, HeyGen, and D-ID work, and what is included for free.
body:
Recording a video takes effort: camera, light, sound, and several takes until every sentence lands. With AI avatars it works differently. You write a text, choose a digital presenter, and the AI creates a video from that. That is popular for training, explainer videos, and product presentations. We introduce three well-known providers. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

Synthesia describes itself as an all-in-one AI video platform for companies. According to the website, you create videos with AI avatars and voiceovers in more than 140 languages. Typical uses are employee training, marketing, and sales. You can get started for free, with no credit card.

Free plan according to the pricing page: 0 € a month, with 500 credits per month, templates, and libraries. You can share content by link, but the videos carry a Synthesia watermark. You can download them and remove the logo only on the paid Starter plan.

HeyGen promotes AI videos in which you yourself play the lead. According to the website, the Avatar V model keeps your avatar looking the same from every angle and with every facial expression. Also new is HeyGen Voice, a speech model of its own.

Free plan according to the pricing page: 0 $ a month. You get 3 videos a month with a watermark, each up to one minute long. On top of that come access to Avatar IV and the Video Agent, a video avatar of your own, more than 500 ready-made presenters, and over 30 languages.

D-ID creates AI videos and interactive agents with digital avatars. A special feature is “Agentic Videos”: according to the provider, passive content becomes interactive experiences in which an avatar responds to questions in real time. New are the V4 Expressive Visual Agents.

Trial according to the pricing page: 14 days free, with 3 minutes for videos, agents, video translation, and the API. Included are more than 100 stock avatars, one personal avatar, and standard voices. During the trial the videos carry a full-screen watermark, and the license is for private use only.

AI avatars save a lot of time on explainer and training videos. The free offers are enough for a try. For videos without a watermark, and for business use, you need a paid plan. You can find more video tools in our tool directory.

seoDescription: An explainer video, a training, or a social media clip, spoken by a digital avatar: how Synthesia, HeyGen, and D-ID work, and what is included for free.

title: Many Shorts from One Long Video: 4 AI Clip Tools Compared
excerpt: A podcast, webinar, or stream: AI finds the best moments and turns them into clips for TikTok, Reels, and YouTube Shorts. Opus Clip, Vizard, Klap, and Submagic.
body:
Short videos are now hard to imagine TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube without. If you already have long videos, such as a podcast, a webinar, or a livestream, you are sitting on a gold mine. AI clip tools pick out the most interesting moments, cut them to portrait format, and add subtitles. We introduce four tools. All details come from the official websites, as of 1 November 2026.

According to the website, OpusClip turns long videos into short clips and, if you want, publishes them to all social platforms with one click. The features include AI editing, AI subtitles, automatic reframing to portrait (Reframe), AI B-Roll, audio enhancement, and AI voiceover.

Good for German-speaking creators: according to the website, videos in English, German, Spanish, French, and Portuguese are supported, among others, about 25 languages in all. Signing up is free, and the Starter plan can be tried without a credit card.

Vizard turns long videos into short clips for TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts, and more, over 30 clips with one click according to the website. New is the Vizard Agent, which the provider describes as a personal video editor. According to the homepage, you can even try Vizard without signing up.

Free plan according to the pricing page: 60 credits per month, where one credit equals one minute of video. You get AI clips, the full video editor, export in 720p, and 3 days of storage. You export without a watermark and in 4K only on the paid Creator plan.

According to the website, Klap creates TikToks, Reels, and Shorts from your long videos with one click. You upload a file or paste a link, for example from Twitch. New is AI Reframe 2: it analyzes your scenes and chooses suitable layouts such as split screen, screen recordings, or gaming views.

According to the website, you can try Klap free with one video, with no credit card. The paid plans are billed by the clips they generate.

Submagic has specialized in subtitles in particular. According to the website, you generate subtitle styles in 123 languages. Submagic also turns one video into several short videos and offers text-based trimming, meaning cutting via the transcript. You can try Submagic for free without a credit card.

Use only videos you have the rights to. If guests appear in your podcast or stream, ask them whether you may publish excerpts. And watch the music in the background: it is often protected by copyright.

AI clip tools save you hours of editing. Start with Vizard’s free plan or a free trial of the other tools, and see which result you like best. You can find more video tools in our tool directory.

title: Better Answers from AI: Writing Prompts for Beginners
excerpt: The answer is only as good as the question. Five simple building blocks get much more from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and the rest. With examples to copy.
body:
You asked the AI a question, and the answer was … well. Too general, too long, or simply off. That often comes from the question, not from the AI. The instruction you give an AI chat is called a “prompt”. With a few simple rules, your prompts get much better. This works with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and most other AI assistants.

Imagine you are giving a new colleague a task. She is smart, but she does not know you. What would she need to know? That is exactly what belongs in your prompt.

1. Role: Who should the AI be? For example: “You are an experienced primary school teacher.”

2. Task: What exactly should happen? For example: “Explain how a rainbow forms.”

3. Context: What do you need this for, and who is it for? For example: “For my eight-year-old son, who likes doing experiments.”

4. Format: What should the answer look like? For example: “In five short sentences at most, then a simple experiment to do at home.”

5. Tone: How should it sound? For example: “Casual, cheerful, without technical terms.”

You do not have to use all five building blocks every time. The more of them you include, the better the answer fits.

Before: “Write an email to my landlord.”

After: “Write a polite, short email to my landlord, Mr. Schulz. The heating in the bathroom has not worked for three days. I want him to send a tradesperson this week. I am at home in the mornings. Tone: friendly, but firm. 120 words at most.”

The second prompt is longer, but you can send the result almost as it is.
